subject: tricks for constraining hyperparameter values to yield plausible survival/recovery values

messages.author: 40e173783f466ae0
messages.subject: tricks for constraining hyperparameter values to yield plausible survival/recovery values
parts:
I'm still working on a recovery model, now including hyperparameters. I'd like to try to set my priors to exclude unrealsitic survival or recovery parameters. I know it doesn't matter much once you have a lot of data, but it's still something I'd like to play around with. Without hyperparameters, I've had success, using truncated, beta, or normal distributions with larger-than-typical precision values. I was just curious if any one had any luck doing this with hyperparameters and if you had any tricks for distributions or mean/precision/shape parameter values.

Thanks

messages.subject: Re: tricks for constraining hyperparameter values to yield plausible survival/recovery values
